verses.1: The capture of Ravana was as futile as trying to grasp the wind, and Pulastya heard the gods speaking of this in heaven.
verses.2: Then, trembling with affection for his son, the greatly resolute great sage Pulastya came to see the lord of Mahishmati.
verses.3: Taking the aerial path, that brahmin, with speed like the wind and valor like the speed of thought, reached the city of Mahishmati.
verses.4: He, Pulastya, entered that city, which resembled Amaravati and was bustling with happy and well-nourished people, just as Brahma would enter Indra's Amaravati.
verses.5: Then, seeing him appear like the sun walking on foot, very difficult to behold, they recognized him and reported his arrival to Arjuna.
verses.6: The lord of Haihayas, understanding from the words that it was Pulastya, placed his folded hands on his head in reverence and went forward to meet the ascetic.
verses.7: His priest, having taken the arghya and madhuparka, went forth in front of the king, just as Brihaspati goes before Indra.
verses.8: Then, Arjuna, seeing that sage approaching like the rising sun, was filled with awe and bowed down, just as Indra bows before the supreme lord.
verses.9: Having offered madhuparka, a cow, water for washing feet, and arghya to Pulastya, the king of kings then spoke to him with a voice choked with joy.
verses.10: "Today, my city Mahishmati has been made equal to Amaravati, because today, O chief of brahmins, I am able to see you, who are so rarely seen."
verses.11: O revered one, today is auspicious for me, my vow is fulfilled, my life is fruitful, and my penance is successful, because I bow to your feet, which are worshipped even by the hosts of gods.
verses.12: O Brahmana, this kingdom, these sons, these wives, and we ourselves are at your disposal; please command us what we should do or what task is to be performed.
verses.13: Having inquired about the welfare of that king, Kartavirya Arjuna, regarding his dharma, sacred fires, and sons, sage Pulastya then spoke to him.
verses.14: O king, whose eyes are like lotus petals and whose face resembles the full moon, your strength is incomparable, by which Dashagriva (Ravana) was conquered by you.
verses.15: That grandson of mine, who is unconquerable in battle and from fear of whom the ocean and the wind stand motionless, has been bound by you in combat.
verses.16: You have diminished my son's fame and spread your own reputation, so now, at my request, release this child Dashanana.
verses.17: Having accepted Pulastya's command, Arjuna spoke not a word, and indeed, the king of kings joyfully released the lord of Rakshasas.
verses.18: Having released Ravana, the enemy of the gods, Arjuna honored him with divine ornaments, garlands, and garments, then, having established a non-violent friendship witnessed by fire and bowed to Pulastya, the son of Brahma, he returned home.
verses.19: The mighty lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, though released by Pulastya, embraced, and offered hospitality, felt ashamed, having been defeated.
verses.20: And also, Pulastya, the son of Brahma and the foremost among sages, having released Dashagriva, indeed went to the world of Brahma.
verses.21: Thus, the mighty Ravana, having experienced humiliation at the hands of Kartavirya, was again released due to the intervention and words of Pulastya.
verses.22: Thus, O delight of the Raghus, there are indeed stronger individuals than the strong, and one who desires their own welfare should never show disrespect towards others.
verses.23: Then, that king of the flesh-eaters, having obtained a truce from Sahasrabahu, again caused the slaughter of kings and roamed all over the earth with arrogance. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 33 ।। Thus ends the thirty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
